display_title: HORIZON-CL5-2027-05-D4-05 On-site robotic and automated techniques for building renovation and new construction – Horizon Europe
call_module_title: HORIZON-CL5-2027-05-D4-05 On-site robotic and automated techniques for building renovation and new construction
executive_summary: Horizon Europe Innovation Action that funds the development and demonstration of on-site robotic and automated techniques for the energy renovation of existing buildings and, optionally, new construction, with at least one technique using 3D printing, attention to worker safety and human-robot collaboration, and at least three demonstrations across building typologies and climates, up to TRL 6-8. Open to consortia under the standard Horizon Europe rules, excluding entities controlled from China; the JRC may join after selection. Lump-sum grant at the Innovation Action rates (70% for for-profit entities, up to 100% for non-profit). Indicative topic budget EUR 20.25 million, around EUR 6.75 million per project, about three projects. Planned opening 5 May 2027; single-stage deadline 15 September 2027.
status_rationale: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027 Part 8 (Climate, Energy and Mobility), pp. 199–201, Specific conditions, Expected Outcome and Scope of HORIZON-CL5-2027-05-D4-05, funds on-site robotic, automated and 3D-printing techniques for building renovation and construction sites, explicitly excluding off-site prefabrication. It does not touch TenneT's field: the work is limited to buildings and construction sites, with no link to grid assets, substations or electricity system operation, and no project file is close to it (Station Veenoord–Boerdijk mentions modular construction, but of a high-voltage station, not of buildings). No project date is set because the call states no start, end or duration.
